subject: Decision sync: traffic-light rollout & rollback plan for BlueHarbor private deployment
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, BlueHarbor CTO <cto@blueharbor.ai>, procurement@blueharbor.ai
Date: 2027-06-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Traffic-light rollout & rollback plan for BlueHarbor private deployment

Team —

Quick sync request to land the minimal decision criteria and rollback play for the BlueHarbor private (VPC + on-prem edge) engagement. We have an internal kickoff with their infra leads next Wed; before that we need an agreed "traffic-light" decision matrix (green/amber/red) that pairs: performance criteria, required staffing, and an explicit rollback trigger.

What I need from each of you by EOD Friday:
- Kimberly: an ops minimal-runbook (oncall slots, escalation path, maintenance windows) that can be handed to customer SREs.
- Karthik: an architecture risk summary with required GPU/VM counts per phase (pilot, scale-1), and the downgrade/quantization-compatible variants we can fall back to.
- Laura: legal/contract asks or necessary SLA exceptions (credits, retention) we should pre-approve for an amber -> green path.

I've attached an initial traffic-light CSV with suggested thresholds and a short MPA from BlueHarbor. Please keep asks tight — customer expects a clear go/no-go grid rather than free-form caveats.

Priyom
Head of Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachments: traffic-light-matrix.csv (draft), blueharbor-mpa.pdf (customer brief)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-05T12:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Traffic-light rollout & rollback plan for BlueHarbor private deployment

Thanks — quick read and a few clarifying points below. I sketched a minimal runbook that we can hand to the customer during pilot. High level:

- Oncall: 1 infra engineer (on-call) + 1 escalation engineer (on-call backup) during business hours for pilot; 24/7 not required for pilot but must be in contract for scale-1.
- Maintenance window: 1x weekly 2-hour window; major upgrades only in amber->green pauses.
- Escalation path: Customer SRE -> Redwood infra oncall -> Redwood dev lead (Karthik) -> exec oncall (Priyom)

Rollback triggers (suggested):
- RED: sustained P50 latency > 2.5x SLA for > 15m OR error rate > 3% for > 10m -> immediate rollback to hosted fallback model (hosted-compat variant).
- AMBER: intermittent latency spikes (1.5x-2.5x) OR tail errors during peak deploy window -> stop rollout, engage drift runbook, increase cache sizes, disable noncritical inference paths.
- GREEN: all perf metrics within thresholds for 24h and successful warmup with production traffic.

Questions for Karthik: the hosted fallback requires re-encoding to a smaller kv-cache format — how long is expected failover time in worst-case? (estimate in minutes). Also attaching runbook-diff.pdf with the short format we can hand off.

Kimberly
Sr. Manager, Infrastructure Ops
Redwood Inference

Attachments: runbook-diff.pdf

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-06T08:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Traffic-light rollout & rollback plan for BlueHarbor private deployment

Adding architecture perspective and rough numbers. TL;DR: pilot capable with modest infra, scale requires additional GPUs and a short warmup window to populate KV caches. Fallback timing depends on cache size and network egress.

Pilot (noncritical traffic):
- 4x A10g-equivalent GPUs across 2 machines (replica=2) for model v1 (8-bit quantized). Expected steady-state token throughput ~ 1200 tps equivalent under conservative batching.
- Recovery/fallback path (hosted-compat) rollback time estimate: 6-12 minutes to switch routing + 3-7 minutes to rehydrate small prefix caches for common paths. Worst-case 20 minutes for cold paths.

Scale-1 (production-ish):
- 12x A10g-equivalent GPUs across 6 machines (replica=3) with autoscale headroom + KV cache warmers. Requires ops staffing (1 infra day shift + 1 escalation at night) for first 72 hours post-cutover.

Downgrade variants: quantized v1 (8-bit) -> quantized v2 (6-bit per-tensor) -> hosted-lite (lower context, aggressive caching). Quality drop expected: 2-4% top-level generation variance between v1->v2. We should add a short eval set to monitor regressions.

Notes / Risks:
- Network egress constraints on their edge cluster may amplify failover time. Need confirmation from BlueHarbor on peering and MTU.
- Database retention for KV cache: if we can't persist warm caches, warmup extends to several hours for cold traffic profiles.

Happy to add this to the traffic-light CSV as numeric thresholds.

Karthik
Principal Architect, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Thanks — the matrix looks useful. A couple quick asks from our side so we can evaluate internally:

1) Can you give a blunt expected downtime window for the RED rollback path? We need this to scope our change freeze and customer notifications.
2) For Amber, what monitoring hooks do you expect BlueHarbor to expose (prometheus endpoints, custom traces)?
3) Procurement: is there a minimal SLA doc we can reference for pilot vs scale?

We can share our peering and MTU info by EOD tomorrow. If you can add the blunt worst-case numbers into the CSV, we'll move faster.

— Maya (CTO)
BlueHarbor Systems

Appreciate the fast replies. Summary and next steps:

- I'll add worst-case rollback numbers from Karthik (20 minutes cold worst-case) into the CSV and mark a RED downtime window of <= 30 minutes for customer comms.
- Kimberly: finalize the runbook and include the explicit switch checklist for hosted fallback. Please ensure the runbook lists the exact routing toggles and cache-warm commands (so customer SREs can follow).
- Laura: propose three pre-approved SLA exceptions (pilot credit, retention window extension, limited exec-oncall) that legal can greenlight quickly.
- Karthik: please append the numeric GPU/replica counts and the expected warm-up minutes to the CSV. Add a single eval metric for quality regression (BLEU-like or embedding drift) so product can gate amber->green.

I'll consolidate into a single nexus doc and circulate to BlueHarbor tomorrow morning before the internal kickoff. If anyone needs a quick 15m to align, ping and I'll set up a call.

Priyom
Head of Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachments: traffic-light-matrix.csv (updated with Karthik numbers)
